newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee extends losses vs forward dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee extends losses vs forward dollar.

text.p: The Indian rupee continued to weaken in the forward dollar market on Monday, dealers said.

Dealers said the primary reason was a reversal of sentiment on the forward dollar earlier this month, coinciding with a weakening of the rupee in the spot dollar market and firming of call money rates to double-digit levels.
Six-month dollar premium, which fell almost to 1.0 rupees earlier this month, opened at 1.63/1.68 rupees on Monday.
The premia rose towards noon to a high of 1.68/1.72 rupees and but closed the day around the opening levels.
Many banks said stop loss limits had been reached. Banks which had built up large oversold positions were getting out of their commitments in view of the rising level of premia.
"It (six-month premia) could go upto 1.90 rupees," said Yeshwant Rao, deputy general manager (forex) at Arvind Mills. But he said the rise in premia would be gradual.
He said the six-month premia would eventually fall to 1.40 rupees. "It will hold at this level," he predicted.
Dealers said the spot dollar market was inactive on Monday in sharp contrast to fluctuations seen last week.
The spot dollar closed at 35.76/77, almost unchanged from the opening level. The day's range was 35.7650/7850 rupees.
"There were (dollar) sellers today," said a dealer. "People are awaiting to see the trend of commercial activity -- would it be demand or supply that will dominate?" he asked.

Most dealers expect dollar demand to outstrip supplies, keeping the rupee under pressure. "There won't be much upside for the rupee because the RBI (Reserve Bank of India) will buy (dollars) at the prevailing levels," said a dealer.
